name: Infernal Pursuit raises melee haste by 3% and shortens root duration by 15% (#2469)
contract: Infernal Pursuit 704992 reads 'Increases your melee haste by $s1% and reduces the duration of root effects against you by $s2%.' Effect 0 is native aura 138 (SPELL_AURA_MOD_MELEE_HASTE), EffectBasePoints 2 with DieSides 1 -> 3, handler AuraEffect::HandleModMeleeSpeedPct (src/server/game/Spells/Auras/SpellAuraEffects.cpp:203,4993) -- a native generic attack-speed aura, fully wired. Effect 1 is native aura 232 (SPELL_AURA_MECHANIC_DURATION_MOD), EffectMiscValue 7 (MECHANIC_ROOT, confirmed at src/server/shared/DataStores/SharedDefines.h:1409), EffectBasePoints -16 with DieSides 1 -> -15 (all verified directly in the installed Spell.dbc). Its handler comment at SpellAuraEffects.cpp:297 reads '232 SPELL_AURA_MECHANIC_DURATION_MOD implement in Unit::CalculateSpellDuration' and is consumed at src/server/game/Entities/Unit/Unit.cpp:12224 via target->GetTotalAuraModifierByMiscValue(SPELL_AURA_MECHANIC_DURATION_MOD, i) inside Unit::ModSpellDuration's per-mechanic loop over a landing harmful spell's mechanic mask -- a real, wired native consumer on the recipient side, not a stub. HARNESS LIMIT: ModSpellDuration's reduction can only be observed on a debuff actually cast on the Knight (Unit::AddAura, used by set_aura, never calls it -- its only callers are the real cast path in Spell.cpp and SpellEffects.cpp). This scenario follows the established Adrenaline precedent (apps/coa-gameplay-test/scenarios/bloodmage-adrenaline.json, same aura type and consuming function) for that same harness limit: it asserts the resolved aura_amount for effect 1 (the value ModSpellDuration would apply) rather than fabricating a self-cast root fixture; the duration reduction on a real incoming root needs a Ghost e2e encounter.
